record.title: Jiangsu sets AI employment monitoring and skills-training targets
record.summary: Jiangsu's provincial government office published a September 29, 2026 employment-policy notice that calls for assessing the employment effects of major policies and public investment and establishing a survey of AI's effects on jobs and skills. For labor-intensive sectors, it says the province will explore minimum human-participation standards and a displacement buffer period. The notice also sets a target of one million person-times of AI-field technical-skills training during the fifteenth Five-Year Plan period. These are announced measures and targets; the notice does not show funding, delivery, implementation or employment effects. The policy predates and is separate from China's later October 16 national AI-employment opinion.
organizations: Jiangsu Department of Human Resources and Social Security
Jiangsu Department of Industry and Information Technology

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Jiangsu's provincial government office published notice Su Zheng Ban Fa [2026] No. 48 on September 29, 2026; the notice is signed September 23.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The notice calls for employment-impact assessment of major policies and public investment and establishes an AI-employment impact survey to track AI adoption, job creation and displacement, and changing skill needs.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: For labor-intensive sectors, the notice says Jiangsu will explore minimum human-participation standards and a displacement buffer period; these are exploratory measures, not established operating rules.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The notice sets a target of one million person-times of continuing education and skills training for AI-field technical workers during the fifteenth Five-Year Plan period.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The notice does not establish that the survey, human-participation standards, buffer periods or training target have been implemented, funded, delivered or associated with employment outcomes.

evidence_gaps.description: The notice describes policy instruments but no subordinate city task lists, implementing rules, appropriations or operating survey were inspected.
No AI-skills training delivery against the one-million-person-time target or employment effects were reported in the inspected source.

brief.importance_rationale: If carried out, Jiangsu's announced package could shape regional assessment of AI's employment effects, labor safeguards and skills provision at scale. The one-million-person-time training target and proposed monitoring measures are consequential regional signals, but the notice supplies no appropriation, delivery or measured outcome.
limitations: The source is a provincial policy notice; it establishes announced measures, not operational implementation or results.
Human-participation standards and displacement buffer periods are described as exploratory, not as rules already in force.
The training figure is one million person-times, not one million distinct workers.
No funding amount, city rollout, survey data, training delivery or employment outcome was verified.
organizations: Jiangsu Department of Human Resources and Social Security
Jiangsu Department of Industry and Information Technology

relationships.summary: Jiangsu's September notice is a distinct provincial AI-employment policy instrument that predates the national State Council opinion dated October 16; it is not evidence of implementing that later opinion.

technical.claimed_result: Jiangsu's notice announces an AI-employment survey, employment-impact assessment, exploratory labor safeguards and a one-million-person-time AI technical-skills training target.
technical.demonstrated_result: The official notice documents policy directions, responsible agencies and a training target. It does not demonstrate execution, appropriations, training delivery, survey results or employment effects.
technical.implementation_status: Notice Su Zheng Ban Fa [2026] No. 48 was signed September 23 and posted September 29, 2026. Several measures assign responsibilities or targets; minimum human-participation standards and displacement buffer periods remain exploratory in the notice. Downstream implementation was not inspected.
technical.mechanism: Jiangsu combines employment-impact assessment in policy and investment review, an AI-employment tracking survey, proposed labor safeguards, AI-field skills training and AI-enabled public employment services.
technical.regime: Provincial policy for Jiangsu, China. It addresses government policy and investment assessment, AI adoption and employment, labor-intensive sectors, AI-related technical skills and public employment services. No implementing sample or delivery population is reported.
technical.reproducibility: Not applicable to a policy notice. The official Chinese text was inspected directly at the cited sections; implementation and effects remain unverified.
technical.strongest_baseline: The notice addresses employment assessment and adaptation alongside Jiangsu's wider employment-policy measures. It predates the State Council's national AI-employment opinion dated October 16, 2026 and should be treated as a distinct provincial instrument, not its implementation.

brief.title: Jiangsu sets AI employment monitoring and skills-training targets
brief.why_it_matters: A large Chinese province has set out specific ways to monitor AI-related job creation and displacement, assess employment effects in policy decisions, and expand AI-skills training. The notice signals a regional policy approach, while leaving implementation and results unproven.
